Subject: Post-signature: Implementation roadmap & MAP for HemisphereAI

Amanda —

Congrats again on the signature. To keep momentum, I put together a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed implementation cadence that embeds the evaluation plan, canary approach, migration windows, and training phases. Attached: HemisphereAI_MAP_v1.xlsx and SOW_outline.pdf.

High-level objectives:
- Goal: staged rollout of Redwood inference into HemisphereAI production with measurable quality parity to your baseline and predictable unit economics.
- Target go-live window: August 11–22 (flexible pending procurement/PO).

Proposed phases (summary):
1) Prep & Provisioning (Week 0): account setup, key exchange, VPC peering verification, baseline tokens and traffic sample capture.
2) Canary (Weeks 1–2): 2-week canary with 5% traffic routing to Redwood dedicated pool; ramp to 20% on successful gates.
3) Migration Cutover (Week 3): phased cutover per region with automatic fallback to baseline model for 2 hours post-cutover.
4) Training & Enablement (ongoing): two 90-minute workshops (engineering + ops), runbook handoff, and a post-rollout lessons session.

Key asks from your side:
- Confirm any blackout/maintenance windows between Aug 4–25.
- Confirm primary PO/contact for procurement.
- Share a small eval prompt set (10–20 prompts) reflecting real queries you want prioritized.

Success criteria (draft):
- Latency: P95 under 450ms for production prompt distribution.
- Error rate: <0.5% request failures.
- Quality: automated eval score not lower than 3% relative drop vs your current baseline (detailed in EvalPromptSet).

Next steps: please review the attached MAP_v1 and SOW_outline. I'm proposing a MAP sync on Monday 2025-07-21 at 10:00 PT — does that work for you?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Amanda, Rachel —

Thanks — looping in some implementation detail so we can lock the MAP during Monday's sync. I've attached the CanaryTestPlan.md and the EvalPromptSet.json referenced in Rachel's note. Below are the technical gates and evaluation plan I propose.

Canary plan (detailed):
- Day 0 (provision): Dedicated pool sized for expected concurrency + 15% buffer. Baseline telemetry collection (latency distribution, token counts).
- Week 1 (ramp): 5% traffic for 48h, then 10% for 72h. Mid-canary quality review at Day 7 using the eval set.
- Week 2 (stress+validation): extend to 20% traffic for 3 days if mid-canary passes. Run synthetic load to validate autoscaling behavior.
- Rollback policy: immediate rollback to your current endpoint if (a) P95 latency > 600ms sustained for 30m, (b) error rate > 1% in a 15m window, or (c) automated eval quality below threshold defined below.

Evaluation plan (metrics + methodology):
- Prompt set: EvalPromptSet.json (20 representative prompts covering short, medium, and long sequences).
- Quality signal: pairwise A/B comparison against your baseline using automated BLEU/ROUGE-adapted scoring plus a small blind human review sample (10 items) for semantic accuracy.
- Pass thresholds: automated metric delta <= 3% degradation; human review must show no systematic hallucination patterns.

Training and runbooks:
- Proposed dates for hands-on workshops: Aug 5 (Engineering deep-dive, 90m) and Aug 7 (SRE runbook + incident response, 60m). I'll lead the engineering session; Marissa will own the runbook and docs handoff.

Attachments:
- CanaryTestPlan.md (detailed canary schedule & rollback scripts)
- EvalPromptSet.json (eval prompts)

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet post-sync to reflect agreed gates and owners.

Jonas Weber
Implementation Lead
Redwood Inference
